newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Gilts must hold 113-11 for further upside.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Gilts must hold 113-11 for further upside.

text.p: September gilts must hold above 113-11/15 on Monday if they are to trade towards the top of their recent range at 113-28, technical analysts said.
But longer term, the top of the market is approaching, and investors should start selling into strength, they added.
"The key for today is that we need to hold above 113-11/15 which is fairly good congestive support," said Marc Ostwald, technical analyst at London Bond Broking.
"If we can hold that, we can trade towards the top of range with initial congestion at 113-25/28 which will probably hold it for the moment."
Charts show the market hit a daily low of 113-11 on June 11 and 113-15 on June 9 and 12. It hit a high of 113-25 on June 5, 113-26 on June 11 and 19 and a low of 113-28 on June 17.
Otswald said if the market did break out above 113-28 it would likely falter around 114-05/08, the highs on June 18 and June 6 and 12 respectively.
"The market is reasonably well supported...but I don't think overall that the trend is positive, it doesn't want to trade outside the range," said Ostwald.
"We're probably near the top end of the market to sell again."
Juliette Clark senior treasury manager at the Royal Bank of Scotland suggested keeping an eye on 113-18, the 38.2 percent retracement of the losses from 114-18.
"A failure to penetrate this barrier will result in a downturn to 113-06 and a period of consolidation will follow," she said in a note for clients.
"But if September manages to establish activity above 113-18 then the upside view will improve and additional gains should follow to 113-25 and then to 113-29/31."
Clark said a move towards this level would entice new buyers into the market, a may allow a recovery to 114-18 this week.
By 0709 GMT the September gilt contract was down 4/32 at 113-12. September short sterling was down three basis points at 93.01 and the December contract was down 0.04 at 92.81.
